agenticWorkflows.head: Agentic workflows
agenticWorkflows.lead: I plan each project as a map of tasks, and AI agents build it ticket by ticket. The maps below are the real ones.

lessons.all: Every workflow, in the developer view

answerFirst.paid: Build tickets were filed the night before the final design (#208). A newsletter provider was swapped after it was already wired in (#242 → #299).

blockedTicket.paid: Otherwise an agent could start from a plan that changed an hour ago. The pick command checks GitHub first and refuses.
blockedTicket.rule: A blocked ticket can't be picked.

hostDecision.paid: A hosting switch slipped in under a lint ticket and was reverted two days later (#377, #378).
hostDecision.rule: Changing host is its own decision.

realDeploy.paid: Four bugs only showed up once the site was deployed (#382, #387, #388, #395).
realDeploy.rule: Test deploy work on a real deploy.

unknownsFirst.paid: Hosting was picked on paper, then changed five times (#186, #244, #302, #377).

lessons.line: Each one cost a real project time. The numbers are the tickets where it happened.

index.head: Built by rules
index.intro: AI agents write most of the code. I write the rules they follow, and every decision is public.
index.lead: Websites for small publications and practices, and the tools that run them.

agents.line: Tests, lint rules and three review agents decide what gets merged. I step in when they ask.

decide.line: Any call that could go either way gets a short report anyone can read.
decide.proof: Keeping Huella Legal's old links working

look.line: Each design starts from a study of award-winning sites.

plan.line: Before the first ticket, I map every task and what it waits on.

prove.line: Tests, accessibility and lint rules run on every change.

index.title: Built by

build.does: Writes the change, then runs lint, types and tests.

pick.does: Takes the next ticket and reads everything it links to.

plan.does: Lists the files to change, each copied from an existing example.

polish.does: Trims comments and checks the docs still match the code.

review.does: Three agents review architecture, correctness and tests at once.

ship.does: Opens the pull request and merges it once CI passes.

board.answer: On one GitHub board for every project, with a label per area.
board.question: Where is work tracked?

comments.answer: One fact the code can't show, in one sentence.
comments.question: How much should a code comment say?

console.answer: No. Any console output fails the build, in the source and in tests.
console.question: Can a stray console message reach production?

visitor.answer: Here, in the visitor view. The developer view is one click away.
visitor.question: Where does someone who doesn't code land on this site?

example.line: A law magazine rebuilt with these five rules.

method.head: Method
method.lead: Every project here follows them. Each one is backed by a check that fails the build, a skill the agents load, or a public record.

accessibility.claim: Pages are tested against WCAG AA in a real browser.

design.claim: Each app is split into layers, and a layer can only use the ones below it.
design.how: Crossing a boundary is a lint error.

lint.claim: Lint rules, some written for this repo.
lint.claimCount: {enabled} lint rules on, {inHouse} of them written for this repo.
lint.how: Turning one off needs a written reason.

observability.claim: The apps report their errors and slow requests.
observability.how: A slow click can be traced to the query behind it.

repository.claim: Repo-wide rules are checked on every commit, push and CI run.
repository.how: No hand-edited version numbers, no leftover TODOs.

tests.claim: Tests, from single functions to full pages in a real browser.
tests.claimCount: {count} test files, from single functions to full pages in a real browser.
tests.how: If coverage drops below the minimum, the build fails.

method.title: Five rules,

agents.body: An agent takes a ticket from plan to merge, and no person reads the code. Any of the {steps} steps can stop and ask me.
agents.title: Let agents write the code.

decide.body: When a call could go either way, I write a short report: the question, the options, what was picked and why. The next person, or agent, reads it instead of asking again.
decide.title: Write decisions down.

look.body: I start each design from sites an awards jury already picked, and measure each one the same way: type, colour, layout.
look.title: Look before drawing.

plan.body: Each project starts from a template with every task the job needs, what each one waits on, and what went wrong last time.
plan.count: {count} lessons from past projects so far.
plan.title: Plan the whole job.

prove.body: These run on every push and again in CI.
prove.title: Check every change.
